All paths below are relative to `/home/daniel/ui-work/runs/202610271-to/sandbox/officehq-tanstack-officefloor/src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/` (written `app/`). Migrations are under `.../src/main/resources/db/migration/` and `.../src/main/java/db/migration/`, and endpoints under `.../src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/`. I changed nothing. Items marked ⚠ are places where code, comments or migrations disagree.

## 1. Settings: storage and dating
- **`SettingRepository.set`** (`setting/SettingRepository.java:400-413`): deletes the row with the same `from_key` (null means 0001-01-01), inserts the new value, and appends a `setting_history` row stamped with the sheet's today. A change to any key in `POLICY_KEYS` also inserts the next `policy_version` (`COALESCE(MAX(version),0)+1`).
- **`isDated`** (`:160-163`): every key is dated except policy-date, grace-days, escalate-after, review-sla, pending-sla, max-open, score-mid, score-high, score-log, period-numbering-from, entry-date, proof-kinds, pot, alert-threshold, fiscal-start-month, parent, default-grade and every `perm-*` key. ⚠ The Javadoc at `:158-159` lists only about half of these.
- **`ChangeSetting`** (`setting/ChangeSetting.java:38-39`): a dated key with no from-date takes the sheet's today, not the beginning of time. Through the API, only values from before V29 or undated keys can have a null from-date. `ValidateSetting:36-37` silently drops a from-date sent for an undated key.
- **`DatedSetting.on(date)`** (`setting/DatedSetting.java:11-19`): returns the value with the latest from-date on or before the date (null counts as earliest). If no value qualifies it returns `start`; a stored blank value returns null. This is one of three hand-copied copies of the same "latest from ≤ date" loop. The others are `Person.gradeOn` (`person/Person.java:95`) and `Person.termsOn` (`:125`), plus a variant in `RateRepository.inForce`.
- **`find(key)`** (`:220`): reads an undated key as `dated(...).on("9999-12-31")`.
- **`datedAsOf` / `lateAsOf` / `capAsOf`** (`:196-217`): give the value as it stood at the end of a date, from `setting_history.on_date`.
- **`policyVersions`** (`:315`): lists versions oldest first. `POLICY_KEYS = rounding, floor, cap, terms, late-pct, clerk-limit` (`:156`). Per-grade keys (`clerk-limit-X`, `terms-X`, `grace-X`) do not create versions. A version is written even when the value does not change. V104/V105 backfilled versions from `setting_history` in id order.

## 2. Sheet setting keys
Format names used below:
- **MONEY** (`ValidateSetting:18`): matches `\d+(\.\d{0,2})?|\.\d{1,2}`, stored at scale 2.
- **DAYS** (`:21`): matches `\d{1,6}`.
- **WHOLE** (`:24`): matches `-?\d{1,6}`.

Line numbers are the constant in `SettingRepository` / the branch in `ValidateSetting`.

| key | dated | default | validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clerk-limit` (:26 / :46) | yes | none (no limit) | blank or MONEY |
| `clerk-limit-<grade>` (:30 / :50) | yes | falls back to sheet value | grade must be one of the sheet's codes; blank or MONEY |
| `proof-threshold`, `proof-threshold-<grade>` (:34, :39 / :55, :59) | yes | none | blank or MONEY |
| `proof-kinds` (:43 / :64) | no | none | comma list of `ProofKind.ALL` (receipt, photo), de-duplicated |
| `note-threshold` (:47 / :72), `review-threshold` (:51 / :76), `cap` (:55 / :80) | yes | none | blank or MONEY |
| `pot` (:58 / :84), `alert-threshold` (:62 / :90) | no | none | blank or MONEY |
| `floor` (:65 / :96) | yes | `DEFAULT_FLOOR` "1.00" (:153) | MONEY; cannot be blank ⚠ (`SettingRequest` says a blank value clears a setting) |
| `late-pct` (:75 / :100) | yes | `DEFAULT_LATE_PCT` "0.00" (:147) | MONEY; cannot be blank |
| `terms` (:68 / :110) | yes | `DEFAULT_TERMS` "14" (:150) | DAYS; cannot be blank |
| `terms-<grade>` (:71 / :116) | yes | sheet terms | blank or DAYS |
| `rounding` (:83 / :104) | yes | none (policy date decides) | blank, `half-up` or `half-even` |
| `policy-date`, `period-numbering-from`, `entry-date` (:79, :87, :91 / :172) | no | today / off / off | blank or ISO date |
| `grace-days` (:95 / :159) | no | off | blank or DAYS (closes periods automatically, `period/AutoClosePeriods.java:25`) |
| `grace-<grade>` (:128 / :165) | yes | 0 | blank or DAYS |
| `escalate-after`, `review-sla`, `pending-sla`, `max-open` (:99-111 / :123-146) | no | off | blank or DAYS |
| `score-mid`, `score-high` (:115, :119 / :147) | no | off | blank or WHOLE (negatives allowed) |
| `score-log` (:123 / :153) | no | off | blank or `on` |
| `fiscal-start-month` (:137 / :184) | no | "1" (:144) | 1 to 12; cannot be blank |
| `default-grade` (:141 / :191) | no | "A" (`defaultGrade` :230) | blank or a grade code. ⚠ The Javadoc says "A, B or C" |
| `parent` (:133 / :197, `ChangeSetting:20-35`) | no | none | not self; the sheet must exist; no cycle (walks `rates.parent` with a seen-set) |
| `perm-<action>` (`Permissions.isKey` / :201) | no | the standing rule | comma list of **clerk and steward only** (:27) |
| anything else | | | refused with "Unknown setting" (:209) |

How each value is looked up:
- **`clerkLimit`, `proofThreshold`** (`:261`, `:271`): the grade's value in force on the claim's date, else the sheet's value on that date.
- **`terms(sheet, grade, date)`** (`:331`): `terms-<grade>`, else sheet terms, else 14.
- **`terms(sheet, person, date)`** (`:338`): the person's own `termsOn`, else the grade's, else the sheet's.
- **`termsToday`** (`:348`): evaluates the terms on the **sheet's today**, whatever the claim's date.
- **`capOn`** (`:305`): the cap in force on the person's latest counting claim date, else on today.
- **`entryDate`** (`:370`): the `entry-date` setting, else the sheet's today.

## 3. Rates
- **Form rules** (`rate/RateForm.check:18-33`): the grade must be one of the sheet's codes; percent is MONEY scaled to 2; from/to are blank (null) or ISO dates; to must not be before from. ⚠ `InvalidRateException:3` still says "grade is not A, B or C". V6 also has a DB check `pct >= 0`.
- **Import** (`ValidateImportRates:19-30`): each non-blank line is `grade,rate,from,to`; more than 4 fields is refused; each line goes through `RateForm.check`; any bad line refuses the whole import; zero lines is refused. `ImportRates:25-35` sets lines in order, each as `RATE_SET` followed by a rollup diff. It has no `TakeRollup` step in the YAML.
- **`RateRepository.set`** (`:177-196`): the existing row for the same grade and from_key is copied to `rate_version`; the new version is old + 1. **Forward-only:** if from is not null and from ≥ the sheet's today (falling back to `LocalDate.now()`), `claims_after` = `MAX(id)` across the **whole claim table, all sheets** (`:181-182`). The new row is appended to `rate_history`.
- **`Rate.forClaim`** (`rate/Rate.java:26-28`): a forward-only rate applies only to claims with id > `claimsAfter`; older claims use `prior`, recursively (built by `withPriors`, `:59-78`).
- **Rate in force on a claim's date** (`RateRepository.inForce:159-171`, via `find:122`): levels are 0 (own sheet), then up to `LEVELS = 3` parents, then the clone source's chain (`chain:88-103`, de-duplicated). At each level it takes the grade's version applicable to the claim with the latest from ≤ date. If that rate's `to < date`, it moves on to the **next level**; it does not fall back to an earlier same-level rate (consistent with V27). It returns null if nothing is found. The grade used is `person.gradeOn(claim.date)`. This lookup is repeated in about 10 places: `SettleClaim:133`, `ApproveClaim:41`, `OpenClaim:65`, `ResettleClaim:35`, `Rollup:86,100,197`, `TakeStatement:83,98`, `PeriodClosing:61`, `RollOver:110`, `ClaimLogRepository:43`, `PreviewRate:41`.
- **As-of view** (`listAsOf` / `ownAsOf:128-144`): uses the last `rate_history` row per key with `on_date ≤ asOf`. Withdrawn rows are excluded.
- **Withdraw** (`ValidateRateWithdrawal:19-31`): **steward only, by `roleOf`, so a delegated steward may withdraw**. `from` is blank or `start` (null) or a date. The sheet must have its own rate for that grade and from (`has`). `RateRepository.withdraw:206-224` deletes the current version and restores the newest `rate_version` (its `claims_after` is kept). If there is no older version, it writes a `withdrawn=TRUE` history row.
- **Preview** (`PreviewRate:25-53`, `ValidateRatePreview`): looks at OPEN/PENDING claims whose person's grade on the claim's date equals the candidate grade. "Now" uses the real in-force rate; "then" applies the candidate on every date. The candidate has no from/to, ignores forward-only and ancestor levels, and uses the current late charge and floor. It returns a count and the summed difference. No role check (GET).

## 4. Due computation: floor, late percent, rounding, grace
- **`Dues.of`** (`claim/Dues.java:39`): `amount × pct / 100`, rounded to 2 decimals with the claim's rounding mode.
- **`Dues.shown`** (`:73-81`): returns `settledDue` if set; else `statedDue` if bound by a statement; else the live figure raised to the floor in force on the claim's date (corrections, i.e. negative amounts, get no floor), plus the late charge.
- **`Dues.charge`** (`:54-67`): zero for corrections, non-open, deferred, or waived claims. Lateness counts from `dueBy + grace` (`lateFrom:23`). For each full 30 days up to today, it adds `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary date × (figure + charge so far). That is compounding, rounded per step.
- **`Late.rounding`** (`:29-34`): uses the `rounding` setting in force on the round date. Otherwise half-up before the `policy-date` and half-even on or after it; a blank policy date means today. The round date is the claim's date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects (`ClaimRepository:26-28`). ⚠ The `charge` Javadoc says "rounded by the policy date"; the code uses the rounding mode first.
- **Grace per grade** (`SettingRepository.grace:384-395`): `grace-<person.gradeOn(claim.date)>` in force on the claim's date; 0 if none. Note `late()` uses the current person record, while `lateAsOf` uses `findAsOf`.

## 5. Terms, due-by, holidays
- **`BusinessDays.isBusinessDay` / `dueBy` / `between`** (`holiday/BusinessDays.java:13-37`): Saturday, Sunday and sheet holidays are not business days. The due-by is the terms-th business day after the date (terms 0 means the date itself). `between` counts business days in (date, dueBy].
- **Adding a claim** (`claim/AddClaim.java:24-28`): due-by = `holidays.dueBy(date, termsToday(person))` (`HolidayRepository.dueBy:43` uses only holidays after the date). `ClaimRepository.add:167` stores `terms = between(date, dueBy, all holidays now)`. The same pattern is in `PasteClaims:121`, `GeneratePlanClaims:64` and `SplitClaim:56`. ⚠ `FindOrAddPerson:49` uses `terms(id, defaultGrade, today)`, i.e. grade terms with no person override. ⚠ V24 and V77 say the due-by follows the terms "in force on its date", but the code uses the terms in force on the sheet's today.
- **Holidays** (`ValidateHoliday:14-23`): must be an ISO date and not already a holiday (DB unique constraint too). There is no remove endpoint. ⚠ The errors are thrown as `InvalidSettingException`.
- **`RefixDueBys` → `ClaimRepository.refixDueBys`** (`:320-333`): for claims not SETTLED, VOID or DELETED, with `due_by_set` false and `due_by ≥ holiday`, the due-by is recomputed from the **current** `claim_date` with the stored terms. ⚠ The Javadocs (`RefixDueBys:7`, `holidays.POST.yml`) omit DELETED and the `due_by_set` exemption. ⚠ V44 says "a holiday added later leaves existing due-by dates as they are", which is now false. ⚠ `redate` (`:303`) "leaves due-by", but a later refix recomputes from the new date, while V45/V51 use the first recorded date.
- **Due-by set directly** (`SetClaimDueBy:23`): steward only. It sets `due_by_set` (V101) so later holiday refixes leave it alone.
- **V45** (`db/migration/V45__business_day_due_by.java:69-80`): walks back over the run of holidays that existed when the claim was created, takes the **calendar**-day count as terms, then re-applies it as **business** days with all current holidays. This applies to every claim, including SETTLED and VOID ones, and overwrites `due_by` on all `claim_history` rows. In effect, old calendar-day terms became business-day terms, so due-bys moved later.
- **V51** (`V51__claim_terms.java:145-151`): `terms = between(firstDate, dueBy, holidays added ≤ created_at)`. ⚠ This disagrees with V45, which used all holidays: a holiday added after the claim but before V45 is counted by V51 as a business day, so the recovered terms are one higher per such holiday.

## 6. Grades
- **`GradeRepository`**: `GRADES = A, B, C` are built in (`:14`), and added grades follow in insertion order (`codes:32`). `CODE = [A-Z]{1,3}` (`:17`).
- **Add** (`ValidateAddGrade:12-17`): must match `CODE` and not already exist. `ensure:52` silently adds grades brought in from another sheet.
- **Retire** (`ValidateRetireGrade`): must be a sheet grade and not already retired. The only effect is `requireChoosable` (`:79`), which refuses that grade for a new person or an edit. Rates, settings and people on the grade are untouched. ⚠ The comments in `InvalidGradeException:3` and `grade-retire.POST.yml` still say "not A, B or C". ⚠ `GradeRequest`'s Javadoc says "retiring", but it is also used for adding. `FindOrAddPerson:44-46` falls back to the hard-coded "A" when the default grade is retired, even if A is retired too.
- **Merge** (`ValidateMergeGrade`; `MergeGrade:39-88`): both must be sheet grades and different. **Steward only, by `roleOf`, checked in Java.** It checks archived itself, because there is no `RefuseViewer` in the YAML. Merging into a retired grade is refused only if somebody would move. It selects people by `p.getGrade()` (the grade on today), gives each the target grade from today, and then `regrade`s every past grade record of theirs retroactively (`PersonRepository.regrade:420`). People who had the merged grade only in the past are not touched.

## 7. Crews
- **`ValidateCrew:12-24`**: name required (trimmed), not used by another crew or a pool, lead required.
- **`AddCrew:18-21`**: the lead must be a person on the sheet. `added_on` = the sheet's today.
- **`AddCrewMember:18-34`**: the crew and person must exist; the person cannot be the lead or already a member. It skips `sheets.open`, and the YAML has no separate validate step.
- **`CrewRepository.list(asOf)`** (`:27`): as-of visibility by `added_on`.
- **On person merge** (`PersonRepository:619-626`): the merged person's leadership moves to the survivor, and duplicate memberships or leader-is-also-member rows are dropped.
- **On transfer away** (`:721`): crews they lead stay with no lead (V78 allows a null lead).

## 8. Notes
- **`ValidateNote`**: text is trimmed and must not be blank. ⚠ The error is thrown as `InvalidSettingException`.
- **`NoteRepository.add`**: `added_on` = the sheet's today. In as-of view, only notes with `added_on ≤ today` are listed (`:27-29`).

## 9. Roles, permissions, delegation and who may do what
**Roles** (`setting/Role.java:7-10`): clerk, steward, viewer, restricted.
- `assignedRoleOf` (`RoleRepository:33`): a user with no row is a clerk.
- `roleOf` (`:28`): steward if a delegation covers the sheet's today (`delegatorOf:40`, latest by id), otherwise the assigned role.
- `ValidateRole:8-19` accepts all four roles. ⚠ The `roles.POST.yml` header and `InvalidSettingException:3` say only clerk or steward are allowed.
- The DB check constraint was widened in V18, V32 and V93.

**`RefuseViewer`** (`setting/RefuseViewer.java:14-19`): the first YAML step on almost every write. It refuses on an archived sheet and refuses viewers by `roleOf`.
- **Missing from:** `bulk-*` (they re-check viewer or archived inline: `BulkSettleClaims:58`, `BulkVoidClaims:53`, `BulkGradePeople:38`, `BulkHoldPeople:36`, `BulkRetirePeople:36`, `BulkOpenClaims:55`, `GeneratePlanClaims:43`), `grade-merge`, period `lock`/`unlock`, `rollover`, `rollover-undo`, claim `unlock`, and sheet `open`.
- `bulk-reassign` and `bulk-redate` rely only on the per-claim checks plus an archived check.

**Permission matrix** (`setting/Permissions.java:23-30, 47-52`): a non-blank `perm-<action>` replaces the standing rule.

| action | standing rule |
|---|---|
| open | clerk, steward |
| settle | clerk, steward |
| void | clerk, steward |
| close | clerk, steward |
| reassign | steward |
| reopen | steward |
| today | clerk, steward, restricted |

⚠ `ValidateSetting` only lets a matrix entry name clerk or steward. Once `perm-today` is set, restricted users can never be given it back.

Where the matrix is enforced:
- open: `OpenClaim:29`, `BulkOpenClaims:56`, `PasteClaims:88`, `SplitClaim:37`
- settle: `SettleClaim:84` (shared with bulk), `JudgePartSettle:18`
- void: `VoidClaim:39`
- reassign: `ReassignClaim:41`
- close: `ClosePeriod:32`, `SoftClosePeriod:30`
- reopen: `ReopenPeriod:22`
- today: `PermitSheetToday:15`

**Hard-coded steward-only checks** (by `roleOf`, so delegated stewards pass):
- **Claims:** `RedateClaim:30`, `SetClaimDueBy:23`, `ReviewClaim:23`, `AssignReview:14`, `WaiveClaim:14`, `ResettleClaim:31`, void of a SETTLED claim within `SETTLED_DAYS` (`VoidClaim:48`), opening a claim for a flagged person (`OpenClaim:78`).
- **People:** `FlagPerson:15`, `MergePerson:28`, `TransferPerson:44`, `ValidateTransferUndo:17`, `CancelStatement:18`.
- **Sheet and periods:** `ArchiveSheet:17`, `CloneSheet:24`, `LockPeriod:19`, `UnlockPeriod:19`, `RollOver:46`, `UndoRollover:29` (also must be the same user who rolled over).
- **Grades and rates:** `MergeGrade:39`, `ValidateRateWithdrawal:19`.

**Approver:**
- `ApproveClaim:32` and `RejectClaim:80` allow a steward or the person's approver (`isApprover:54`, an exact user-name match).
- Approve applies four-eyes (not the user who opened or last edited the claim) and the proof rule. Reject requires a reason.
- ⚠ `people/{id}/approver.POST` is guarded only by `RefuseViewer`. Any clerk can name themselves a person's approver and then approve that person's PENDING claims.

**Clerk limit** (`SettleClaim:99-106`): applies only when `roleOf` is exactly clerk. It uses the grade's limit, else the sheet's, in force on the claim's date. If the due exceeds the limit, the claim goes to PENDING instead of SETTLED. Restricted users and delegated stewards bypass it. ⚠ The class Javadoc (`:25`) says the limit is taken "on the sheet's today", but the code uses the claim's date.

**Delegation:**
- `ValidateDelegation:19`: only an **assigned** steward may delegate; a delegated steward cannot. User required; dates blank (today) or ISO; to must not be before from.
- ⚠ V35 says a delegate "acts as a steward in every rule"; delegating is the exception.
- Audit lines from a delegate get `for=<delegator>` (`Audit.java:60-72`).

**Restricted:** the only server-side difference from a clerk is that restricted is missing from the standing open, settle, void and close lists. The people-list filtering (only their crews and themselves) exists **only in the frontend** (`src/main/frontend/features/people/People.tsx:502, 992`). The server returns everyone.

**Left open to any non-viewer, including clerks and restricted users:**
- `SetRole` (`roles.POST.yml`): anyone can make themselves steward.
- `ChangeSetting`: the permission matrix, clerk limit, terms, etc.
- `SetRate` and `ImportRates`
- grade add and retire, holidays, crews, notes, `approver`

## How scattered and tangled it is
The rules are spread across three layers: YAML step order (which endpoints get `RefuseViewer`), validator classes, and per-action Java checks. There are three overlapping authorisation schemes (the `Permissions` matrix, hard-coded `Role.STEWARD` checks, and approver or delegation special cases), and the same rate, floor and late-charge lookup is re-implemented in about 10 classes. Many Javadocs, YAML headers and migration comments describe older behaviour (A/B/C-only grades, clerk/steward-only roles, holidays never moving due-bys, terms taken on the claim's date, clerk limit on today). The resulting gaps are real: any clerk can promote themselves to steward or appoint themselves approver, and the restricted role is enforced only in the UI.

## 1. Settings: storage and dating
- **`SettingRepository.set`** (`setting/SettingRepository.java:400-413`): deletes the row with the same `from_key` (null means 0001-01-01), inserts the new value, and appends a `setting_history` row stamped with the sheet's today. A change to any key in `POLICY_KEYS` also inserts the next `policy_version` (`COALESCE(MAX(version),0)+1`).
- **`isDated`** (`:160-163`): every key is dated except policy-date, grace-days, escalate-after, review-sla, pending-sla, max-open, score-mid, score-high, score-log, period-numbering-from, entry-date, proof-kinds, pot, alert-threshold, fiscal-start-month, parent, default-grade and every `perm-*` key. ⚠ The Javadoc at `:158-159` lists only about half of these.
- **`ChangeSetting`** (`setting/ChangeSetting.java:38-39`): a dated key with no from-date takes the sheet's today, not the beginning of time. Through the API, only values from before V29 or undated keys can have a null from-date. `ValidateSetting:36-37` silently drops a from-date sent for an undated key.
- **`DatedSetting.on(date)`** (`setting/DatedSetting.java:11-19`): returns the value with the latest from-date on or before the date (null counts as earliest). If no value qualifies it returns `start`; a stored blank value returns null. This is one of three hand-copied copies of the same "latest from ≤ date" loop. The others are `Person.gradeOn` (`person/Person.java:95`) and `Person.termsOn` (`:125`), plus a variant in `RateRepository.inForce`.
- **`find(key)`** (`:220`): reads an undated key as `dated(...).on("9999-12-31")`.
- **`datedAsOf` / `lateAsOf` / `capAsOf`** (`:196-217`): give the value as it stood at the end of a date, from `setting_history.on_date`.
- **`policyVersions`** (`:315`): lists versions oldest first. `POLICY_KEYS = rounding, floor, cap, terms, late-pct, clerk-limit` (`:156`). Per-grade keys (`clerk-limit-X`, `terms-X`, `grace-X`) do not create versions. A version is written even when the value does not change. V104/V105 backfilled versions from `setting_history` in id order.

## 2. Sheet setting keys
Format names used below:
- **MONEY** (`ValidateSetting:18`): matches `\d+(\.\d{0,2})?|\.\d{1,2}`, stored at scale 2.
- **DAYS** (`:21`): matches `\d{1,6}`.
- **WHOLE** (`:24`): matches `-?\d{1,6}`.

Line numbers are the constant in `SettingRepository` / the branch in `ValidateSetting`.

| key | dated | default | validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clerk-limit` (:26 / :46) | yes | none (no limit) | blank or MONEY |
| `clerk-limit-<grade>` (:30 / :50) | yes | falls back to sheet value | grade must be one of the sheet's codes; blank or MONEY |
| `proof-threshold`, `proof-threshold-<grade>` (:34, :39 / :55, :59) | yes | none | blank or MONEY |
| `proof-kinds` (:43 / :64) | no | none | comma list of `ProofKind.ALL` (receipt, photo), de-duplicated |
| `note-threshold` (:47 / :72), `review-threshold` (:51 / :76), `cap` (:55 / :80) | yes | none | blank or MONEY |
| `pot` (:58 / :84), `alert-threshold` (:62 / :90) | no | none | blank or MONEY |
| `floor` (:65 / :96) | yes | `DEFAULT_FLOOR` "1.00" (:153) | MONEY; cannot be blank ⚠ (`SettingRequest` says a blank value clears a setting) |
| `late-pct` (:75 / :100) | yes | `DEFAULT_LATE_PCT` "0.00" (:147) | MONEY; cannot be blank |
| `terms` (:68 / :110) | yes | `DEFAULT_TERMS` "14" (:150) | DAYS; cannot be blank |
| `terms-<grade>` (:71 / :116) | yes | sheet terms | blank or DAYS |
| `rounding` (:83 / :104) | yes | none (policy date decides) | blank, `half-up` or `half-even` |
| `policy-date`, `period-numbering-from`, `entry-date` (:79, :87, :91 / :172) | no | today / off / off | blank or ISO date |
| `grace-days` (:95 / :159) | no | off | blank or DAYS (closes periods automatically, `period/AutoClosePeriods.java:25`) |
| `grace-<grade>` (:128 / :165) | yes | 0 | blank or DAYS |
| `escalate-after`, `review-sla`, `pending-sla`, `max-open` (:99-111 / :123-146) | no | off | blank or DAYS |
| `score-mid`, `score-high` (:115, :119 / :147) | no | off | blank or WHOLE (negatives allowed) |
| `score-log` (:123 / :153) | no | off | blank or `on` |
| `fiscal-start-month` (:137 / :184) | no | "1" (:144) | 1 to 12; cannot be blank |
| `default-grade` (:141 / :191) | no | "A" (`defaultGrade` :230) | blank or a grade code. ⚠ The Javadoc says "A, B or C" |
| `parent` (:133 / :197, `ChangeSetting:20-35`) | no | none | not self; the sheet must exist; no cycle (walks `rates.parent` with a seen-set) |
| `perm-<action>` (`Permissions.isKey` / :201) | no | the standing rule | comma list of **clerk and steward only** (:27) |
| anything else | | | refused with "Unknown setting" (:209) |

How each value is looked up:
- **`clerkLimit`, `proofThreshold`** (`:261`, `:271`): the grade's value in force on the claim's date, else the sheet's value on that date.
- **`terms(sheet, grade, date)`** (`:331`): `terms-<grade>`, else sheet terms, else 14.
- **`terms(sheet, person, date)`** (`:338`): the person's own `termsOn`, else the grade's, else the sheet's.
- **`termsToday`** (`:348`): evaluates the terms on the **sheet's today**, whatever the claim's date.
- **`capOn`** (`:305`): the cap in force on the person's latest counting claim date, else on today.
- **`entryDate`** (`:370`): the `entry-date` setting, else the sheet's today.

## 3. Rates
- **Form rules** (`rate/RateForm.check:18-33`): the grade must be one of the sheet's codes; percent is MONEY scaled to 2; from/to are blank (null) or ISO dates; to must not be before from. ⚠ `InvalidRateException:3` still says "grade is not A, B or C". V6 also has a DB check `pct >= 0`.
- **Import** (`ValidateImportRates:19-30`): each non-blank line is `grade,rate,from,to`; more than 4 fields is refused; each line goes through `RateForm.check`; any bad line refuses the whole import; zero lines is refused. `ImportRates:25-35` sets lines in order, each as `RATE_SET` followed by a rollup diff. It has no `TakeRollup` step in the YAML.
- **`RateRepository.set`** (`:177-196`): the existing row for the same grade and from_key is copied to `rate_version`; the new version is old + 1. **Forward-only:** if from is not null and from ≥ the sheet's today (falling back to `LocalDate.now()`), `claims_after` = `MAX(id)` across the **whole claim table, all sheets** (`:181-182`). The new row is appended to `rate_history`.
- **`Rate.forClaim`** (`rate/Rate.java:26-28`): a forward-only rate applies only to claims with id > `claimsAfter`; older claims use `prior`, recursively (built by `withPriors`, `:59-78`).
- **Rate in force on a claim's date** (`RateRepository.inForce:159-171`, via `find:122`): levels are 0 (own sheet), then up to `LEVELS = 3` parents, then the clone source's chain (`chain:88-103`, de-duplicated). At each level it takes the grade's version applicable to the claim with the latest from ≤ date. If that rate's `to < date`, it moves on to the **next level**; it does not fall back to an earlier same-level rate (consistent with V27). It returns null if nothing is found. The grade used is `person.gradeOn(claim.date)`. This lookup is repeated in about 10 places: `SettleClaim:133`, `ApproveClaim:41`, `OpenClaim:65`, `ResettleClaim:35`, `Rollup:86,100,197`, `TakeStatement:83,98`, `PeriodClosing:61`, `RollOver:110`, `ClaimLogRepository:43`, `PreviewRate:41`.
- **As-of view** (`listAsOf` / `ownAsOf:128-144`): uses the last `rate_history` row per key with `on_date ≤ asOf`. Withdrawn rows are excluded.
- **Withdraw** (`ValidateRateWithdrawal:19-31`): **steward only, by `roleOf`, so a delegated steward may withdraw**. `from` is blank or `start` (null) or a date. The sheet must have its own rate for that grade and from (`has`). `RateRepository.withdraw:206-224` deletes the current version and restores the newest `rate_version` (its `claims_after` is kept). If there is no older version, it writes a `withdrawn=TRUE` history row.
- **Preview** (`PreviewRate:25-53`, `ValidateRatePreview`): looks at OPEN/PENDING claims whose person's grade on the claim's date equals the candidate grade. "Now" uses the real in-force rate; "then" applies the candidate on every date. The candidate has no from/to, ignores forward-only and ancestor levels, and uses the current late charge and floor. It returns a count and the summed difference. No role check (GET).

## 4. Due computation: floor, late percent, rounding, grace
- **`Dues.of`** (`claim/Dues.java:39`): `amount × pct / 100`, rounded to 2 decimals with the claim's rounding mode.
- **`Dues.shown`** (`:73-81`): returns `settledDue` if set; else `statedDue` if bound by a statement; else the live figure raised to the floor in force on the claim's date (corrections, i.e. negative amounts, get no floor), plus the late charge.
- **`Dues.charge`** (`:54-67`): zero for corrections, non-open, deferred, or waived claims. Lateness counts from `dueBy + grace` (`lateFrom:23`). For each full 30 days up to today, it adds `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary date × (figure + charge so far). That is compounding, rounded per step.
- **`Late.rounding`** (`:29-34`): uses the `rounding` setting in force on the round date. Otherwise half-up before the `policy-date` and half-even on or after it; a blank policy date means today. The round date is the claim's date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects (`ClaimRepository:26-28`). ⚠ The `charge` Javadoc says "rounded by the policy date"; the code uses the rounding mode first.
- **Grace per grade** (`SettingRepository.grace:384-395`): `grace-<person.gradeOn(claim.date)>` in force on the claim's date; 0 if none. Note `late()` uses the current person record, while `lateAsOf` uses `findAsOf`.

## 5. Terms, due-by, holidays
- **`BusinessDays.isBusinessDay` / `dueBy` / `between`** (`holiday/BusinessDays.java:13-37`): Saturday, Sunday and sheet holidays are not business days. The due-by is the terms-th business day after the date (terms 0 means the date itself). `between` counts business days in (date, dueBy].
- **Adding a claim** (`claim/AddClaim.java:24-28`): due-by = `holidays.dueBy(date, termsToday(person))` (`HolidayRepository.dueBy:43` uses only holidays after the date). `ClaimRepository.add:167` stores `terms = between(date, dueBy, all holidays now)`. The same pattern is in `PasteClaims:121`, `GeneratePlanClaims:64` and `SplitClaim:56`. ⚠ `FindOrAddPerson:49` uses `terms(id, defaultGrade, today)`, i.e. grade terms with no person override. ⚠ V24 and V77 say the due-by follows the terms "in force on its date", but the code uses the terms in force on the sheet's today.
- **Holidays** (`ValidateHoliday:14-23`): must be an ISO date and not already a holiday (DB unique constraint too). There is no remove endpoint. ⚠ The errors are thrown as `InvalidSettingException`.
- **`RefixDueBys` → `ClaimRepository.refixDueBys`** (`:320-333`): for claims not SETTLED, VOID or DELETED, with `due_by_set` false and `due_by ≥ holiday`, the due-by is recomputed from the **current** `claim_date` with the stored terms. ⚠ The Javadocs (`RefixDueBys:7`, `holidays.POST.yml`) omit DELETED and the `due_by_set` exemption. ⚠ V44 says "a holiday added later leaves existing due-by dates as they are", which is now false. ⚠ `redate` (`:303`) "leaves due-by", but a later refix recomputes from the new date, while V45/V51 use the first recorded date.
- **Due-by set directly** (`SetClaimDueBy:23`): steward only. It sets `due_by_set` (V101) so later holiday refixes leave it alone.
- **V45** (`db/migration/V45__business_day_due_by.java:69-80`): walks back over the run of holidays that existed when the claim was created, takes the **calendar**-day count as terms, then re-applies it as **business** days with all current holidays. This applies to every claim, including SETTLED and VOID ones, and overwrites `due_by` on all `claim_history` rows. In effect, old calendar-day terms became business-day terms, so due-bys moved later.
- **V51** (`V51__claim_terms.java:145-151`): `terms = between(firstDate, dueBy, holidays added ≤ created_at)`. ⚠ This disagrees with V45, which used all holidays: a holiday added after the claim but before V45 is counted by V51 as a business day, so the recovered terms are one higher per such holiday.

## 6. Grades
- **`GradeRepository`**: `GRADES = A, B, C` are built in (`:14`), and added grades follow in insertion order (`codes:32`). `CODE = [A-Z]{1,3}` (`:17`).
- **Add** (`ValidateAddGrade:12-17`): must match `CODE` and not already exist. `ensure:52` silently adds grades brought in from another sheet.
- **Retire** (`ValidateRetireGrade`): must be a sheet grade and not already retired. The only effect is `requireChoosable` (`:79`), which refuses that grade for a new person or an edit. Rates, settings and people on the grade are untouched. ⚠ The comments in `InvalidGradeException:3` and `grade-retire.POST.yml` still say "not A, B or C". ⚠ `GradeRequest`'s Javadoc says "retiring", but it is also used for adding. `FindOrAddPerson:44-46` falls back to the hard-coded "A" when the default grade is retired, even if A is retired too.
- **Merge** (`ValidateMergeGrade`; `MergeGrade:39-88`): both must be sheet grades and different. **Steward only, by `roleOf`, checked in Java.** It checks archived itself, because there is no `RefuseViewer` in the YAML. Merging into a retired grade is refused only if somebody would move. It selects people by `p.getGrade()` (the grade on today), gives each the target grade from today, and then `regrade`s every past grade record of theirs retroactively (`PersonRepository.regrade:420`). People who had the merged grade only in the past are not touched.

## 7. Crews
- **`ValidateCrew:12-24`**: name required (trimmed), not used by another crew or a pool, lead required.
- **`AddCrew:18-21`**: the lead must be a person on the sheet. `added_on` = the sheet's today.
- **`AddCrewMember:18-34`**: the crew and person must exist; the person cannot be the lead or already a member. It skips `sheets.open`, and the YAML has no separate validate step.
- **`CrewRepository.list(asOf)`** (`:27`): as-of visibility by `added_on`.
- **On person merge** (`PersonRepository:619-626`): the merged person's leadership moves to the survivor, and duplicate memberships or leader-is-also-member rows are dropped.
- **On transfer away** (`:721`): crews they lead stay with no lead (V78 allows a null lead).

## 8. Notes
- **`ValidateNote`**: text is trimmed and must not be blank. ⚠ The error is thrown as `InvalidSettingException`.
- **`NoteRepository.add`**: `added_on` = the sheet's today. In as-of view, only notes with `added_on ≤ today` are listed (`:27-29`).

## 9. Roles, permissions, delegation and who may do what
**Roles** (`setting/Role.java:7-10`): clerk, steward, viewer, restricted.
- `assignedRoleOf` (`RoleRepository:33`): a user with no row is a clerk.
- `roleOf` (`:28`): steward if a delegation covers the sheet's today (`delegatorOf:40`, latest by id), otherwise the assigned role.
- `ValidateRole:8-19` accepts all four roles. ⚠ The `roles.POST.yml` header and `InvalidSettingException:3` say only clerk or steward are allowed.
- The DB check constraint was widened in V18, V32 and V93.

**`RefuseViewer`** (`setting/RefuseViewer.java:14-19`): the first YAML step on almost every write. It refuses on an archived sheet and refuses viewers by `roleOf`.
- **Missing from:** `bulk-*` (they re-check viewer or archived inline: `BulkSettleClaims:58`, `BulkVoidClaims:53`, `BulkGradePeople:38`, `BulkHoldPeople:36`, `BulkRetirePeople:36`, `BulkOpenClaims:55`, `GeneratePlanClaims:43`), `grade-merge`, period `lock`/`unlock`, `rollover`, `rollover-undo`, claim `unlock`, and sheet `open`.
- `bulk-reassign` and `bulk-redate` rely only on the per-claim checks plus an archived check.

**Permission matrix** (`setting/Permissions.java:23-30, 47-52`): a non-blank `perm-<action>` replaces the standing rule.

| action | standing rule |
|---|---|
| open | clerk, steward |
| settle | clerk, steward |
| void | clerk, steward |
| close | clerk, steward |
| reassign | steward |
| reopen | steward |
| today | clerk, steward, restricted |

⚠ `ValidateSetting` only lets a matrix entry name clerk or steward. Once `perm-today` is set, restricted users can never be given it back.

Where the matrix is enforced:
- open: `OpenClaim:29`, `BulkOpenClaims:56`, `PasteClaims:88`, `SplitClaim:37`
- settle: `SettleClaim:84` (shared with bulk), `JudgePartSettle:18`
- void: `VoidClaim:39`
- reassign: `ReassignClaim:41`
- close: `ClosePeriod:32`, `SoftClosePeriod:30`
- reopen: `ReopenPeriod:22`
- today: `PermitSheetToday:15`

**Hard-coded steward-only checks** (by `roleOf`, so delegated stewards pass):
- **Claims:** `RedateClaim:30`, `SetClaimDueBy:23`, `ReviewClaim:23`, `AssignReview:14`, `WaiveClaim:14`, `ResettleClaim:31`, void of a SETTLED claim within `SETTLED_DAYS` (`VoidClaim:48`), opening a claim for a flagged person (`OpenClaim:78`).
- **People:** `FlagPerson:15`, `MergePerson:28`, `TransferPerson:44`, `ValidateTransferUndo:17`, `CancelStatement:18`.
- **Sheet and periods:** `ArchiveSheet:17`, `CloneSheet:24`, `LockPeriod:19`, `UnlockPeriod:19`, `RollOver:46`, `UndoRollover:29` (also must be the same user who rolled over).
- **Grades and rates:** `MergeGrade:39`, `ValidateRateWithdrawal:19`.

**Approver:**
- `ApproveClaim:32` and `RejectClaim:80` allow a steward or the person's approver (`isApprover:54`, an exact user-name match).
- Approve applies four-eyes (not the user who opened or last edited the claim) and the proof rule. Reject requires a reason.
- ⚠ `people/{id}/approver.POST` is guarded only by `RefuseViewer`. Any clerk can name themselves a person's approver and then approve that person's PENDING claims.

**Clerk limit** (`SettleClaim:99-106`): applies only when `roleOf` is exactly clerk. It uses the grade's limit, else the sheet's, in force on the claim's date. If the due exceeds the limit, the claim goes to PENDING instead of SETTLED. Restricted users and delegated stewards bypass it. ⚠ The class Javadoc (`:25`) says the limit is taken "on the sheet's today", but the code uses the claim's date.

**Delegation:**
- `ValidateDelegation:19`: only an **assigned** steward may delegate; a delegated steward cannot. User required; dates blank (today) or ISO; to must not be before from.
- ⚠ V35 says a delegate "acts as a steward in every rule"; delegating is the exception.
- Audit lines from a delegate get `for=<delegator>` (`Audit.java:60-72`).

**Restricted:** the only server-side difference from a clerk is that restricted is missing from the standing open, settle, void and close lists. The people-list filtering (only their crews and themselves) exists **only in the frontend** (`src/main/frontend/features/people/People.tsx:502, 992`). The server returns everyone.

**Left open to any non-viewer, including clerks and restricted users:**
- `SetRole` (`roles.POST.yml`): anyone can make themselves steward.
- `ChangeSetting`: the permission matrix, clerk limit, terms, etc.
- `SetRate` and `ImportRates`
- grade add and retire, holidays, crews, notes, `approver`

## How scattered and tangled it is
The rules are spread across three layers: YAML step order (which endpoints get `RefuseViewer`), validator classes, and per-action Java checks. There are three overlapping authorisation schemes (the `Permissions` matrix, hard-coded `Role.STEWARD` checks, and approver or delegation special cases), and the same rate, floor and late-charge lookup is re-implemented in about 10 classes. Many Javadocs, YAML headers and migration comments describe older behaviour (A/B/C-only grades, clerk/steward-only roles, holidays never moving due-bys, terms taken on the claim's date, clerk limit on today). The resulting gaps are real: any clerk can promote themselves to steward or appoint themselves approver, and the restricted role is enforced only in the UI.

content.text: Settings, rates and roles are done. One helper is left: pools, plans, imports and bulk actions.

I've catalogued every rule in the requested areas below, with file:line references. Paths are relative to `/home/daniel/ui-work/runs/202610271-to/sandbox/officehq-tanstack-officefloor/src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`, and YAML paths to `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/`. **[DUP]** marks a rule written in more than one place. **[CONTRA]** marks a comment that says something different from the code. **[GAP]** marks a check that applies in one route but not another, or a behaviour nothing documents.

## Pools (`pool/`)
- **ValidatePool** `pool/ValidatePool.java:12-21`: refuses a blank name, or one already used by a pool or a crew. The name is trimmed but compared case-sensitively (`name = ?`), unlike person names, which ignore case.
- **AddPool** `pool/AddPool.java:15`: `sheets.open` silently creates the sheet if it has never been loaded.
- **AddPoolMember**, member must exist: `AddPoolMember.java:34-53` refuses an unknown pool, no member named, or a person or pool that is not on the sheet. Crew pools have negative ids, so `nameOf` treats them as "No such pool", which is how "nothing can be added to a crew pool" is enforced.
- **AddPoolMember**, share: `:22,54-61` the share must match `\d+(\.\d{1,2})?` and be more than 0 and at most 100.00.
- **AddPoolMember**, dates: `:62-66,94-105` from and to are optional, and a to-date before the from-date is refused.
- **AddPoolMember**, person already in pool: `:69-71` refused regardless of dates (`hasMember`, `PoolRepository:326`), so a person can't rejoin a pool for a later date range.
- **AddPoolMember**, nested pools: `:76-89` refuses a pool that would contain itself through any chain or is already a member of a pool, and limits a chain to 3 levels (`MAX_DEPTH`, counted with `height()`).
- **PoolRepository.asOf** `:126-182`, total share: the sum of current members' shares. A member is current when its dates include today (or the as-of date). Retired members still count; members outside their dates count as 0. `balanced` means the total is exactly 100.00.
- **cutOf** `:251-268`, which pot a pool cuts: a top-level pool cuts the sheet's pot; a nested pool cuts its own cut in the parent pool. A pool only gets cuts when its total is exactly 100.00 and it has a pot.
- **cut** `:277-311`, who gets a cut:
  - A member gets a cut only if current, not retired, and not under a hold in force on today (or the as-of date). Holds are read at `:159-163`.
  - Retired or held members get 0.00 and their share is shared out among the rest (it is left out of the divisor).
  - Members outside their dates get "" (no cut).
  - If every current member is retired, every member gets "".
  - Each cut is pot × share ÷ (sum of the cutting members' shares), rounded half-even to 2 decimals.
  - The rounding remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut (the latest-added member wins a tie), otherwise to the last cutting member with a non-zero share.
  - If everyone is held, all cuts are 0.00 and the cuts no longer add up to the pot.
- **retired()** `:186-201`: a person counts as retired from the moment `retired_from` is set, even for a future date. So a future retirement already removes their pool cut.
- **crewPools** `:217-246`: each crew becomes a pool. The lead and members share 100.00 equally, with the remainder on the lead. Crew pools are always marked balanced and are never nested. A crew with no members has a total of 0.00.
- **list / freeze / thaw** `:41-116`: period cuts are worked out for every period whose to-date is on or before today. Closed or soft-closed periods instead show the cuts frozen when they were closed (`period_pool_cut`).
- **cutTotals** `:91-99`: a person's cut total is the sum of their non-blank cuts across all pools, crew pools included.
- **moveMembers** (used by merge) `:370-378`: when both people are in a pool, the from-person's share is added to the other's and the from-person's dates are dropped. Nothing checks that the total stays at 100, so a merge can leave a pool unbalanced.

## Plans (`plan/`)
- **ValidatePlan** `plan/ValidatePlan.java:19-42`:
  - The amount goes through `ClaimForm.check`, so it has up to 2 decimals and 0 is allowed.
  - Exactly one of "every N days" or "day of month" must be given. Every is 1-9 digits and at least 1; day is 1-31.
  - Start and end must be dates, and the end may not be before the start.
  - **[CONTRA]** The "A plan's amount is not negative" check (`:25`) can never run. `ClaimForm` already refuses a negative amount with no claim to correct ("must name the claim it corrects", `claim/ClaimForm.java`). The same dead check is in `ValidatePlanAmount.java:20`. **[DUP]**
- **AddPlan** `AddPlan.java:14`: a target sheet must be a descendant of the person's sheet. Whether it is archived is not checked.
- **Plan.dates** `Plan.java:31-48`:
  - Every-N plans run from the start every N days.
  - Day-of-month plans use that day each month from the start month, falling back to the month's last day, and skip dates before the start.
  - Dates inside a pause are skipped, not postponed.
- **PlanPause.skips** `PlanPause.java:9-11`: a pause covers dates on or after the pause day and before the resume day. Pausing and resuming on the same day skips nothing.
- **Pause/Resume** `PausePlan.java:14`, `ResumePlan.java:14`: pausing a paused plan, or resuming a running one, is refused. Both use the sheet's today.
- **ListedPlan.of** `ListedPlan.java:14-15`: next dates are the first 5 plan dates after today, up to the end, without pauses. It doesn't exclude dates already made.
- **GeneratePlanClaims** `GeneratePlanClaims.java:40-83`:
  - Refused on an archived sheet. A viewer gets `made=0` and nothing is written. Roles on the target sheet are not checked.
  - Dates run up to the earlier of the end and today, inclusive.
  - A date is skipped if it is already made (`plan_claim`; a date stays made even if its claim is later voided) or the person is retired before it.
  - Due-by = `holidays.dueBy(date, termsToday)`. If it falls in a closed period the date is skipped and retried next time.
  - Each claim is DRAFT with an empty note, marked late entry when its due-by is in a soft-closed period, and logged with CLAIM_ADDED (plus LATE_ENTRY).

## Pools (`pool/`)
- **ValidatePool** `pool/ValidatePool.java:12-21`: refuses a blank name, or one already used by a pool or a crew. The name is trimmed but compared case-sensitively (`name = ?`), unlike person names, which ignore case.

- **AddPoolMember**, member must exist: `AddPoolMember.java:34-53` refuses an unknown pool, no member named, or a person or pool that is not on the sheet. Crew pools have negative ids, so `nameOf` treats them as "No such pool", which is how "nothing can be added to a crew pool" is enforced.
- **AddPoolMember**, share: `:22,54-61` the share must match `\d+(\.\d{1,2})?` and be more than 0 and at most 100.00.
- **AddPoolMember**, dates: `:62-66,94-105` from and to are optional, and a to-date before the from-date is refused.
- **AddPoolMember**, person already in pool: `:69-71` refused regardless of dates (`hasMember`, `PoolRepository:326`), so a person can't rejoin a pool for a later date range.
- **AddPoolMember**, nested pools: `:76-89` refuses a pool that would contain itself through any chain or is already a member of a pool, and limits a chain to 3 levels (`MAX_DEPTH`, counted with `height()`).

- **cutOf** `:251-268`, which pot a pool cuts: a top-level pool cuts the sheet's pot; a nested pool cuts its own cut in the parent pool. A pool only gets cuts when its total is exactly 100.00 and it has a pot.
- **cut** `:277-311`, who gets a cut:
  - A member gets a cut only if current, not retired, and not under a hold in force on today (or the as-of date). Holds are read at `:159-163`.
  - Retired or held members get 0.00 and their share is shared out among the rest (it is left out of the divisor).
  - Members outside their dates get "" (no cut).
  - If every current member is retired, every member gets "".
  - Each cut is pot × share ÷ (sum of the cutting members' shares), rounded half-even to 2 decimals.
  - The rounding remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut (the latest-added member wins a tie), otherwise to the last cutting member with a non-zero share.
  - If everyone is held, all cuts are 0.00 and the cuts no longer add up to the pot.
- **retired()** `:186-201`: a person counts as retired from the moment `retired_from` is set, even for a future date. So a future retirement already removes their pool cut.
- **crewPools** `:217-246`: each crew becomes a pool. The lead and members share 100.00 equally, with the remainder on the lead. Crew pools are always marked balanced and are never nested. A crew with no members has a total of 0.00.
- **list / freeze / thaw** `:41-116`: period cuts are worked out for every period whose to-date is on or before today. Closed or soft-closed periods instead show the cuts frozen when they were closed (`period_pool_cut`).

## Person import
- **ValidateImport** `person/ValidateImport.java:26-46`:
  - Each line is `name,grade,terms,contact` (split into at most 4 fields). A blank grade means the sheet's default grade.
  - Each line is checked with `PersonForm.check` (`PersonForm.java:14-52`): name required, grade must be one of the sheet's codes, terms 1-5 digits, contact trimmed, lower-cased and at most 200 characters.
  - A name (case-insensitive) or contact repeated within the import is refused, as is an import with no lines.
- **ImportPeople** `ImportPeople.java`, checked up front:
  - A retired grade is refused for a new person or a grade change (`:42-44`).
  - A new person is refused if the name is used in the tree (`:46`) or the contact is used on the sheet (`:49`).
  - A matched person is refused if two lines match them (for example one by name, one by alias) (`:54`), if their existing name or any alias clashes in the tree (`:57`), or if the contact belongs to someone else (`:61`).
- **ImportPeople**, writing:
  - New people are added with terms and contact (PERSON_ADDED).
  - Matched people are updated (PERSON_EDITED) with a version-conflict check on update. Terms and contact change only when the line gives them, and a grade change takes effect from today (`:79-97`).
  - Rollup lines follow each line.
  - Counts: `added` and `updated`.
- **[CONTRA]/[GAP]**:
  - A blank grade on a matched person becomes the default grade, which **regrades** them.
  - Import doesn't call `ApplyPerson`, so it skips the name-taken and version checks and never touches tags. `ApplyPerson.java:35` clears tags when none are given; import leaves them.
  - Import has no archived check of its own; `RefuseViewer` in the YAML guards that.

## Merge and undo merge
- **ValidateMerge** `ValidateMerge.java:10`: the person to merge into is required.
- **MergePerson** `MergePerson.java:28-44`:
  - Steward only (hard-coded role, not the permission matrix).
  - Refused for merging a person into themselves, a target not on the sheet, or either person retired (even with a future retirement date).
  - Order of work: `claims.moveAll`, then `pools.moveMembers`, then `periods.moveTotals`, then `people.merge(undoable=true)`.
- **ClaimRepository.moveAll** `claim/ClaimRepository.java:249-258`: claims move in the order added, become the newest in the list, and keep their numbers, dates and statement binding.
- **PeriodRepository.moveTotals** `period/PeriodRepository.java:218-237`: adds the from-person's period totals and carried amounts into the other's **and** does the same with period openings. **[CONTRA]** MergePerson's javadoc only mentions "closed periods' fixed totals".
- **PersonRepository.merge** `person/PersonRepository.java:546-645`:
  - The from-person's name and aliases become the other's aliases.
  - Their patrons are added to the other's (no repeats, never the other themselves).
  - Anyone who named them as patron names the other instead, with duplicates removed.
  - Their statements are placed before the other's, the counts are added, and the other's last statement stays theirs (`Person.absorbStatements:262`).
  - Their holds, watches, grades, terms and retirement history are deleted.
  - Their **plans and crews move** to the other; crew membership is deduplicated and the other is removed from crews they lead.
  - **[CONTRA]** MergePerson's javadoc says only "holds, watchers, contact" are dropped and says nothing about plans or crews.
- **UndoMerge** `UndoMerge.java:22-33`:
  - Only the **last** merge into the person can be undone, and only if it isn't already undone and is undoable (merges made by transfer are not).
  - Only the user who made it, and only on the same sheet-today.
  - The person's saved rows (person, grades, terms, history, retirement, holds, watches) are put back at the end of the list (`PersonRepository.undoMerge:680-710`). Their own aliases return and the alias made from their name is deleted.
  - Claims still on the other person move back as they are now (`ClaimRepository.moveBack:262`).
  - Patron, pool, period-total, statement, plan and crew changes stay.
  - **[GAP]** The restored person row brings back its old `statement_count` while the other person keeps the absorbed count, so statements are counted twice. The merger doesn't need to still be a steward.

## Transfer
- **ValidateTransfer** `ValidateTransfer.java:10`: a target sheet id is required (trimmed).
- **TransferPerson** `TransferPerson.java:44-88`:
  - Steward only; refused for the same sheet, a retired person, or an archived target.
  - The target person is matched by name or any alias. More than one match is refused, as is a retired match.
  - When there's no match, a contact already on the target sheet is refused.
  - **[GAP]** A target that was never loaded is not archived, so `sheets.open(to)` (`:73`) **creates it**. Any id is accepted.
  - The person's grades are added to the target sheet (`grades.ensure`).
  - Claims move with `transferAll` and are renumbered on the target in order first opened (`ClaimRepository.transferAll:277-295`: reference, lock, settle batch and number dropped; logs, comments, lines, shares and history moved).
  - With a match, the arrival is placed under a stand-in name `#merging-<id>` and merged with `undoable=false`.
- **PersonRepository.transfer** `:713-746`:
  - Patron links in both directions, holds, watches, pool and crew memberships are dropped; crews they lead lose their lead.
  - Statements are parked in `person_left` and the count reset to 0, or kept when merging.
  - Period totals and openings are deleted.
  - Grades, terms, retirement history, aliases and **plans** move. **[GAP]** The plans' target sheets are not re-checked, and TransferPerson's javadoc doesn't mention plans.
- **ValidateTransferUndo** `ValidateTransferUndo.java:17-26`: steward only, the person must have arrived by transfer, and only on the arrival day. It then re-runs the whole of TransferPerson (so a person retired since arriving can't be sent back) and `RestoreStatements` (`PersonRepository:751`).

## Bulk person actions
- **ValidateBulkRetire / Hold / Grade**: no one selected is refused, as is a date that isn't a date. Hold also refuses to before from (`ValidateBulkHold.java:21`); grade must be one of the sheet's grades (`ValidateBulkGrade.java:22`).
- **BulkRetirePeople** `BulkRetirePeople.java:33-57`:
  - Archived sheet is refused; a viewer gets 0.
  - People are processed in list order, ids not on the sheet are skipped, and from defaults to today.
  - **[GAP]** People already retired are re-retired with the new date and counted. The single `RetirePerson` also doesn't check this; `UnretirePerson` does refuse someone not retired.
- **BulkHoldPeople** `BulkHoldPeople.java:33-59`: the to < defaulted-from check is repeated here **[DUP]** (also in `ValidateBulkHold`, `HoldPerson:14`, `ValidateHold:15`). Overlapping holds are allowed.
- **BulkGradePeople** `BulkGradePeople.java:44-76`: refused up front if the grade is retired and anyone would actually receive it. A grade is only given when there's a from-date or it differs from the current one.
  - **[GAP]** Everyone selected is counted and gets a PERSON_EDITED line even when nothing changed.
  - **[CONTRA]** `bulk-grade.POST.yml` says "a grade not A, B or C"; the grades are per-sheet. `Person.java:7` also says "(A, B or C)".
- The archived and viewer checks are inside these classes because their YAML has no `RefuseViewer` guard.

## Holds, retirement, aliases, patrons, watch, flags, contact, tags
- **Hold.covers** `Hold.java:7`: both ends inclusive. For pools, what matters is a hold in force on today (or the as-of date) and added by then (`PoolRepository:159`).
  - **[CONTRA]** `Person.java:11` and `Person.countsLive:224-228` say a hold leaves nothing out of the totals and only affects pools, while `people/{personId}/hold.POST.yml` says OPEN claims within a hold "count in no live total".
- **Person.retiredBefore** `Person.java:247-250`: a claim dated **after** the retire date is refused (one on the retire date is allowed). A past retirement refuses dates strictly between its from and to (`Retirement.refuses:7`).
- **Person.isRetiredReached** `:200`: from today ≥ retire date, open unbound claims leave the live totals.
- **UnretirePerson** `:11`: a person who isn't retired is refused. The retirement is kept as a past one ending today.
- **AddAlias** `AddAlias.java:13`: an alias equal to any name or alias on the sheet (the person's own name included) or anywhere in the tree is refused. **[CONTRA]** `aliases.POST.yml` mentions only the sheet, not the tree.
- **AddPatron** `AddPatron.java:14-23`: self, someone not on the sheet, or an existing patron is refused. There's no cycle check and no retirement check.
- **WatchPerson / WatchRepository.set** `WatchRepository.java:30-41`: per user and idempotent; `changed=false` means no audit line. Viewers are still blocked by `RefuseViewer` even though a watch only affects the user.
- **FlagPerson** `FlagPerson.java:15-20`: steward only; the reason is required (`ValidateFlag:14`). Until defaults to today, and a date in the past is accepted.
  - In force while today ≤ until (`Person.isFlagged:302`).
  - While in force, only a steward can open the person's claims (`OpenClaim.requireFlagSteward:74`, used by bulk open and paste).
- **Contact**: trimmed, lower-cased, at most 200 characters (`PersonForm:46`), and unique per sheet (`PersonRepository.contactTaken:353`). **[DUP]** The check appears 5 times: `AddPerson:22`, `ApplyPerson:30`, `ImportPeople:49,61`, `TransferPerson:70` (only when not merging).
- **Tags**: `ClaimForm.tags` trims, lower-cases, removes duplicates and sorts. Used tags are registered in `sheet_tag` by **[DUP]** `useTags` in both `PersonRepository:459` and `ClaimRepository`. Transfer registers claim tags on the target sheet but not the person's own tags.

## Bulk claim actions
All of them sort the selection by person list order, newest claim first, and count `refused = selected − done`, so an id not on the sheet counts as refused.
- **BulkOpenClaims** `claim/BulkOpenClaims.java:55-88`:
  - Every claim is refused if the sheet is archived or the permission matrix doesn't allow OPEN.
  - Per claim: flag/steward, period open, `opensTo` (REVIEW refused; a DRAFT above the review threshold goes to REVIEW), note threshold, period cap, max open. A failing claim is skipped.
  - **[GAP]** `ClaimStatus.moveTo(OPEN)` allows PENDING → OPEN (`ClaimStatus.java:14`), so bulk open can move a PENDING claim back to OPEN without approval.
  - **[CONTRA]** The javadoc (`:24`) says each is "numbered in turn", but opening doesn't number. The javadoc also doesn't list the max-open check.
- **BulkSettleClaims** `BulkSettleClaims.java:58-95`: **all or nothing**.
  - Everything is refused if the sheet is archived, a selected id isn't on the sheet, or the user is a viewer (hard-coded, **[DUP]** of the permission matrix), or if any claim fails `SettleClaim.settle`.
  - `SettleClaim.settle` (`:63-92`) checks: matrix SETTLE, period open, status OPEN, not deferred, four eyes (not the user who opened it or last edited it), proof threshold, and the clerk limit (above it goes to PENDING, which counts as settled).
  - On success: the next batch number goes on every claim, numbering happens at settle, watchers are notified, and a BATCH_SETTLED line gives the count and the sum of the SETTLED claims' frozen dues.
  - **[CONTRA]** The javadoc lists only some of these refusals (no deferred, proof or clerk-limit).
- **BulkVoidClaims** `BulkVoidClaims.java:53-76`: everything is refused when archived or the user is a viewer (hard-coded). Per claim `VoidClaim.move` (`VoidClaim.java:17-48`):
  - When the sheet has void reasons, one of them is required.
  - A SETTLED claim can be voided only by a steward within 7 days of settling, and is marked as a reversal.
  - Any other claim needs matrix VOID, an open period, and an allowed status change.
- **BulkRedateClaims** `BulkRedateClaims.java:51-72`: archived refuses all. Per claim `RedateClaim.redate` (`:16-38`): steward only, status OPEN or PENDING, a valid date, an open due-by period, and not after the person's retirement. The due-by and number stay. An invalid date is not checked up front, so every claim is refused one by one.
- **BulkReassignClaims** `BulkReassignClaims.java:40-73`: archived refuses all. Per claim `ReassignClaim.reassign` (`:27-51`): matrix REASSIGN, status DRAFT/OPEN/PENDING, an open period, a target that exists, and a target not retired before the claim's date. The statement binding is dropped and a numbered claim is renumbered.
  - **[GAP]** The "not its own person" check is only in `ReassignClaim.move:17`, not in the shared static. **Bulk reassign to the claim's current person succeeds**, renumbering it and logging from=X to=X.

**How scattered it is:** The rules are spread across three layers that partly overlap: the YAML guards (`RefuseViewer`), the per-endpoint Validate/Do classes, and the repositories. Repository methods like `PersonRepository.merge`/`transfer` and `PoolRepository.cut` hold key policy (what is dropped or moved, who gets a cut) that the javadocs above them don't fully describe. Checks such as contact uniqueness, hold date order, viewer/archived refusals, max-open and due-by/closed-period are re-written in 2-5 places with small differences (hard-coded viewer vs the permission matrix, quick-add's grade A fallback vs import's refusal, the reassign self-check only in the single route), so the javadocs and YAML comments have already drifted from the code in at least a dozen places.

# Figures the sheet shows, and the rules behind them I changed nothing. I read the claim and person code myself: `Claim`, `Dues`, `ClaimStatus`, `ClaimNumbers`, the open, settle, approve and void steps, `Person`, and the front end's `rates/api.ts` and `claims/api.ts`. Four read-only helpers went through periods and statements, settings/rates/roles, pools/plans/imports/bulk actions, and the rest of the front end. I spot-checked their findings where they touch the core, but not every line they cite. ⚠ marks a place where comments and code disagree. **Read this first:** almost every money figure on screen is worked out in the browser, in `rates/api.ts` and `claims/api.ts`. The server keeps its own Java copy of the same rules (`Dues`, `Rollup`, `Person.countsLive`). It uses that copy to freeze figures when a claim is settled, a statement is taken or a period is closed, and for the audit lines. ## 1. Figures and rules ### Per claim (`claims/PersonClaims.tsx`) - **`claim-due`**: the front end's `claimDue` (`rates/api.ts:148`), mirrored by Java `Dues.shown`. 1. If the claim has a **`settledDue`** (fixed when it was settled), that is shown. 2. Otherwise, if a statement bound it (**`stated`**), its **`statedDue`** is shown (null shows as `n/a`). 3. Otherwise the figure is live: `amount × rate / 100`, rounded to 2 decimals (`dueOf` / `Dues.of`). - The rate is the one in force on the claim's date (`rateOn` / `RateRepository.find`), for the grade the person had on that date (`gradeOn`). - It searches the sheet's own rates first, then up to 3 parent levels. A rate past its to-date moves the search up a level. - A forward-only rate applies only to claims with an id above **`claimsAfter`**. Older claims use its **`prior`**. 4. The figure is then raised to at least the **`floor`** in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). A correction (negative amount) gets no floor. 5. Then the **late charge** (`lateCharge` / `Dues.charge`) is added on top. - It is charged for each full 30 days past **`lateFrom`**, which is `dueBy` plus the grace days (`grace-` for the grade on the claim's date). - Each step uses the `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary. It compounds on the figure plus the charges before it, and each step is rounded. - There is no charge on a correction, a claim that is not open, a **deferred** claim, or a **waived** one. - **Rounding** (`roundsHalfUp` / `Late.rounding`): the `rounding` setting in force on the claim's round date. When none is set, half-up before the `policy-date` and half-even from it on (a blank policy date means today). - The **round date** is the claim's own date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects. - ⚠ The `SettleClaim` Javadoc says the floor is applied *after* the late charge; the code applies it before. - **`claim-due-by`**: fixed when the claim is added. It is the terms-th business day after its date, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays (`BusinessDays.dueBy`). - The terms are the person's own, else their grade's (`terms-`), else the sheet's (default 14), all as in force on the **sheet's today** (`termsToday`). - ⚠ `Claim.java` and migrations V24/V77 say "terms in force on the claim's date". - Adding a holiday works it out again (`refixDueBys`), except for SETTLED, VOID and DELETED claims, and claims whose due-by a steward set directly (`due_by_set`). - **`claim-overdue`** (`isOverdue`): the claim is open, not deferred, and `lateFrom < today`. - **`claim-status`** (`ClaimStatus.moveTo`): the claim moves DRAFT → OPEN, or to REVIEW when its due is above `review-threshold`. - OPEN → SETTLED, or PENDING when a clerk settles it above the clerk limit. PENDING → SETTLED by approval, or back to OPEN by rejection. - DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING or REVIEW → VOID. DRAFT → DELETED, and back to DRAFT only on the same sheet-today it was deleted. - **`isOpen`** = OPEN or PENDING. **`isCounting`/`counts`** = OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED. - **`claim-number`** (`ClaimNumbers`) is given when the claim is settled or approved. - While `period-numbering-from` is on or before today, the number is `-`, or `X-` when the due-by falls in no period. - Otherwise it is `FY-`, a sequence shared across the sheet's tree, by the fiscal year its due-by falls in (`fiscal-start-month`). - A voided claim keeps its number. A reassigned claim is renumbered. - ⚠ `ClaimStatus`, `Claim`, `PasteClaims`, `BulkOpenClaims` and the front-end type all still say "numbered when opened". - **`claim-deferred`**: computed in SQL in `ClaimRepository.COLUMNS`. It is true when the status is OPEN, VOID or SETTLED, the claim is not bound by a statement, and `deferred_until > today`. - **`claim-period`**: the period that contains the claim's **due-by** (not its date). - **`claim-stated`, `-waived`, `-held`, `-late-entry`**: shown as stored. - **`held`** is display only; a held claim still counts everywhere. - **`lateEntry`** means the claim was added while its due-by period was soft-closed. - **`claim-review-late`, `claim-pending-late`**: the front end reads the day the claim went to REVIEW or PENDING out of the status-log text, and compares it plus `review-sla` / `pending-sla` with today. - **`claim-policy`**: how many policy versions have a from-date on or before the claim's date. - **`claim-proofs`, `claim-proofs-receipt/photo`**: receipts are `proofs − photoProofs`. - **`claim-shares`**: the claim's shares. A holder's part of a live claim is `amount × share × the rate of the holder's own grade`. A settled claim's part is `settledDue × share`, rounded half-even. ### Per person (`people/People.tsx`) - **Which claims count** (`liveClaims` / `Person.countsLive`, `leftOutLive`, `countsClaimed`): claims that count, minus deferred ones, minus open claims no statement bound once the person's retirement date has been reached (`isRetiredReached`). A **hold** leaves nothing out of the totals; it only matters for pool cuts. ⚠ `hold.POST.yml`, `ClosePeriod` and `TakeStatement` say otherwise. - **`person-claimed`**: the sum of those claims' amounts, minus claims that correct another. - **`person-due-total`** (`personDue` / `Rollup.of`): the sum of the claims' dues, plus the parts the person holds of others' claims, minus the parts others hold of theirs. - It is capped at the `cap` in force on the date of their latest counting claim, minus their pool **cut total**, and never below 0 (`capLessCuts`). - It shows **`n/a`** when their grade today has no rate today, no claim keeps a frozen, bound or still-priced figure, and they hold no part of another claim. - **`person-excess`**: the due-total before the cap, minus the cap. - **`person-settled-total`, `person-open-total`** (`splitDues`). - **`person-aged-0-30/31-60/61`**: open dues grouped by days since the claim date. - **`person-overdue-count/-total`**: the count and sum of dues of their overdue claims. - **`person-claims-OPEN-count` / `-SETTLED-count`**: counted over all their claims, not just the live ones. - **`person-score`**: settled total (corrections left out) ÷ 100, minus 5 per overdue claim, rounded half-even to a whole number. **`person-band`** is HIGH, MID or LOW against `score-mid` / `score-high`. - **`person-active`**: they have an open live claim dated within the last 30 days. - **`person-backing`**: for each patron, their SETTLED `settledDue` over the last 90 days times their share, rounded half-even. Shares split 100 equally (`patronShares`), with the remainder going to the first-named patron. - **`person-cut-total`**: the sum of their pool cuts (`PoolRepository.cut`). - A pool cuts only when its shares total exactly 100.00 and it has a pot. - A member gets a cut only if they are current, not retired and not held. Retired or held members get 0.00, and their share goes to the rest. - The rounding remainder goes to the smallest cut. - A future retirement date already removes the cut. - **`person-period-

-due-total` / `-carried`**: - For a closed or soft-closed period, the figure frozen by `PeriodClosing.fixNow`. - Otherwise the front end works it out live, using each claim's status at the period end, read by regex from the status log. - Carried is the person's opening balance plus open claims from earlier periods. - **Statement fields** (`person-statement-count`, `-stated-total`, `-statement-date`): - `TakeStatement` binds each live claim to its current due. Any claim not live is unbound. - When the statement is taken now, the total it computes is thrown away and Rollup's due-total is stored instead. An as-of statement keeps its own total, which ignores shares. - Cancelling a statement (steward only) unbinds every bound claim and does not restore earlier bindings. - **Flags and other fields**: - **`person-flag-shown`**: shown while today is on or before the flag's until-date. While in force, only a steward may open the person's claims. - **`person-retired`**: true whenever a retirement date is set. - `-grade` is the grade in force today. `-terms`, `-contact`, `-clashing`, `-origin` and `-approver` are shown as stored. - **Sheet totals** (`rollup-*`, `header-*`, `consolidated-*`): `trimmedSum` drops the single highest and lowest figure when there are 3 or more. **`rollup-claimed-total` is not trimmed**, nor are the aged totals. ### What is frozen, and when - **Settle** (`SettleClaim`): `settledDue` = the due shown at that moment, late charge included. - "Settle as of" a date freezes the due as an as-of view of that day works it out. - With no rate, nothing is fixed and the due stays live. - **Resettle** (steward) fixes it again at today's figure. - **Approve** (`ApproveClaim`): freezes the due the same way. It is the same code, copied inline. - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`): binds `statedDue` on each claim and keeps the person's stated total. - **Close or soft-close a period** (`PeriodClosing.fixNow`): freezes per-person totals, carried figures and pool cuts. - Its late charge is priced at the sheet's **today**, not the period end. It applies no cap and no shares, unlike Rollup. - **Auto-close** runs when today changes and `grace-days` is set. - **Reopen** (permission `reopen`, refused while the period is locked) drops the frozen figures. - **Changing the sheet's today** writes a SNAPSHOT of each person's due-total, an as-of copy of the schema, and releases every editor lock. - **Rollover** (steward) makes next year's months and puts open figures in as openings, using a *third* copy of the due loop (`RollOver.openFigures`), which leaves out existing openings. **Undo rollover** does not reopen the periods the rollover soft-closed. ### What a closed period changes - `PeriodRepository.requireOpen` refuses about 20 claim actions when the claim's **due-by** falls in a closed period. Soft-closed periods are not blocked; claims added to one are only marked late entry. - A period **cap** limits how many open claims a person may have in it; it is checked only when a claim is opened. ### Who may do what - **Roles** (`RoleRepository.roleOf`): clerk (the default), steward, viewer, restricted. An active **delegation** makes a user a steward. - **`RefuseViewer`**: a YAML guard on most writes. It refuses viewers and archived sheets, but it is missing on several routes, including the bulk actions, grade merge, period lock/unlock and rollover. - **The `Permissions` matrix**, which a `perm-` setting can override: - open, settle, void, close: clerk and steward - reassign, reopen: steward - today: clerk, steward and restricted - **Hard-coded steward-only actions**: re-date, set due-by, review, assign review, waive, resettle, void a SETTLED claim within 7 days (`VoidClaim.SETTLED_DAYS`), flag, merge, transfer, cancel a statement, lock/unlock, rollover, archive, clone, withdraw a rate, merge grades. - **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim or last edited it may not settle or approve it. - **Approve and reject**: a steward, or the person's **approver**. - **Clerk limit**: when a clerk settles a claim whose due is above `clerk-limit[-]` (as in force on the claim's date), it goes to PENDING instead. ⚠ The Javadoc says "on today". - **Thresholds** checked against the claim's due: - `proof-threshold`: no settle or approve without proofs, or without one of each kind when `proof-kinds` is set. - `note-threshold`: no open with an empty note. - `max-open`: a limit on each person's open claims. - **Gaps:** any clerk can set roles (including making themselves steward), name themselves a person's approver, or change settings. The restricted role is only filtered in the UI. ### What a date decides - **Retirement**: a claim dated *after* the retire date is refused. Once today reaches it, the person's unbound open claims leave the totals. - **Defaults**: a blank claim date means `entry-date`, else today. - **Dated settings** (`DatedSetting.on`): floor, late-pct, terms, cap, the thresholds and rounding all go by the claim's date. Grade and terms go by `gradeOn` / `termsOn`. - **Statements** can be taken as of a past date. ### Imports, paste, holds - **Person import** (`ImportPeople`): new people are added, matched people (by name or alias) are updated. - All or nothing. - A blank grade means the default grade, which **regrades** a person who already exists. - Any name clash in the tree or reused contact refuses the whole import. - **Paste** (`PasteClaims`): all or nothing. - It matches an existing DRAFT by date and note, otherwise adds a new claim. - Then it opens every claim as the open button would, so some may go to REVIEW. - Negative lines are always refused. - **Rate import**: all or nothing. A rate dated today or later is forward-only. - **Openings import**: *adds* to the stored openings, even on closed periods. - **Holds** (person or claim): affect only pool cuts. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It is scattered and tangled. No new developer could pick it up from one place. - **Every figure rule exists twice.** The browser computes what you see, and Java recomputes it in four slightly different loops (Rollup, TakeStatement, PeriodClosing, RollOver) with different cap, share and date rules. - **The same lookups are pasted all over.** The rate/floor/late lookup appears in about 10 classes. - **Permissions come from three schemes**: the matrix, hard-coded steward checks, and YAML guards. - **The comments have drifted.** Doc comments, YAML headers and migration notes contradict the code in more than a dozen places, for example when a claim is numbered, which terms fix the due-by, and what a hold does.
