I read the claim and person code myself: `Claim`, `Dues`, `ClaimStatus`, `ClaimNumbers`, the open, settle, approve and void steps, `Person`, and the front end's `rates/api.ts` and `claims/api.ts`. Four read-only helpers went through periods and statements, settings/rates/roles, pools/plans/imports/bulk actions, and the rest of the front end. I spot-checked their findings where they touch the core, but not every line they cite. ⚠ marks a place where comments and code disagree. **Read this first:** almost every money figure on screen is worked out in the browser, in `rates/api.ts` and `claims/api.ts`. The server keeps its own Java copy of the same rules (`Dues`, `Rollup`, `Person.countsLive`). It uses that copy to freeze figures when a claim is settled, a statement is taken or a period is closed, and for the audit lines. ## 1. Figures and rules ### Per claim (`claims/PersonClaims.tsx`) - **`claim-due`**: the front end's `claimDue` (`rates/api.ts:148`), mirrored by Java `Dues.shown`. 1. If the claim has a **`settledDue`** (fixed when it was settled), that is shown. 2. Otherwise, if a statement bound it (**`stated`**), its **`statedDue`** is shown (null shows as `n/a`). 3. Otherwise the figure is live: `amount × rate / 100`, rounded to 2 decimals (`dueOf` / `Dues.of`). - The rate is the one in force on the claim's date (`rateOn` / `RateRepository.find`), for the grade the person had on that date (`gradeOn`). - It searches the sheet's own rates first, then up to 3 parent levels. A rate past its to-date moves the search up a level. - A forward-only rate applies only to claims with an id above **`claimsAfter`**. Older claims use its **`prior`**. 4. The figure is then raised to at least the **`floor`** in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). A correction (negative amount) gets no floor. 5. Then the **late charge** (`lateCharge` / `Dues.charge`) is added on top. - It is charged for each full 30 days past **`lateFrom`**, which is `dueBy` plus the grace days (`grace-` for the grade on the claim's date). - Each step uses the `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary. It compounds on the figure plus the charges before it, and each step is rounded. - There is no charge on a correction, a claim that is not open, a **deferred** claim, or a **waived** one. - **Rounding** (`roundsHalfUp` / `Late.rounding`): the `rounding` setting in force on the claim's round date. When none is set, half-up before the `policy-date` and half-even from it on (a blank policy date means today). - The **round date** is the claim's own date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects. - ⚠ The `SettleClaim` Javadoc says the floor is applied *after* the late charge; the code applies it before. - **`claim-due-by`**: fixed when the claim is added. It is the terms-th business day after its date, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays (`BusinessDays.dueBy`). - The terms are the person's own, else their grade's (`terms-`), else the sheet's (default 14), all as in force on the **sheet's today** (`termsToday`). - ⚠ `Claim.java` and migrations V24/V77 say "terms in force on the claim's date". - Adding a holiday works it out again (`refixDueBys`), except for SETTLED, VOID and DELETED claims, and claims whose due-by a steward set directly (`due_by_set`). - **`claim-overdue`** (`isOverdue`): the claim is open, not deferred, and `lateFrom < today`. - **`claim-status`** (`ClaimStatus.moveTo`): the claim moves DRAFT → OPEN, or to REVIEW when its due is above `review-threshold`. - OPEN → SETTLED, or PENDING when a clerk settles it above the clerk limit. PENDING → SETTLED by approval, or back to OPEN by rejection. - DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING or REVIEW → VOID. DRAFT → DELETED, and back to DRAFT only on the same sheet-today it was deleted. - **`isOpen`** = OPEN or PENDING. **`isCounting`/`counts`** = OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED. - **`claim-number`** (`ClaimNumbers`) is given when the claim is settled or approved. - While `period-numbering-from` is on or before today, the number is `-`, or `X-` when the due-by falls in no period. - Otherwise it is `FY-`, a sequence shared across the sheet's tree, by the fiscal year its due-by falls in (`fiscal-start-month`). - A voided claim keeps its number. A reassigned claim is renumbered. - ⚠ `ClaimStatus`, `Claim`, `PasteClaims`, `BulkOpenClaims` and the front-end type all still say "numbered when opened". - **`claim-deferred`**: computed in SQL in `ClaimRepository.COLUMNS`. It is true when the status is OPEN, VOID or SETTLED, the claim is not bound by a statement, and `deferred_until > today`. - **`claim-period`**: the period that contains the claim's **due-by** (not its date). - **`claim-stated`, `-waived`, `-held`, `-late-entry`**: shown as stored. - **`held`** is display only; a held claim still counts everywhere. - **`lateEntry`** means the claim was added while its due-by period was soft-closed. - **`claim-review-late`, `claim-pending-late`**: the front end reads the day the claim went to REVIEW or PENDING out of the status-log text, and compares it plus `review-sla` / `pending-sla` with today. - **`claim-policy`**: how many policy versions have a from-date on or before the claim's date. - **`claim-proofs`, `claim-proofs-receipt/photo`**: receipts are `proofs − photoProofs`. - **`claim-shares`**: the claim's shares. A holder's part of a live claim is `amount × share × the rate of the holder's own grade`. A settled claim's part is `settledDue × share`, rounded half-even. ### Per person (`people/People.tsx`) - **Which claims count** (`liveClaims` / `Person.countsLive`, `leftOutLive`, `countsClaimed`): claims that count, minus deferred ones, minus open claims no statement bound once the person's retirement date has been reached (`isRetiredReached`). A **hold** leaves nothing out of the totals; it only matters for pool cuts. ⚠ `hold.POST.yml`, `ClosePeriod` and `TakeStatement` say otherwise. - **`person-claimed`**: the sum of those claims' amounts, minus claims that correct another. - **`person-due-total`** (`personDue` / `Rollup.of`): the sum of the claims' dues, plus the parts the person holds of others' claims, minus the parts others hold of theirs. - It is capped at the `cap` in force on the date of their latest counting claim, minus their pool **cut total**, and never below 0 (`capLessCuts`). - It shows **`n/a`** when their grade today has no rate today, no claim keeps a frozen, bound or still-priced figure, and they hold no part of another claim. - **`person-excess`**: the due-total before the cap, minus the cap. - **`person-settled-total`, `person-open-total`** (`splitDues`). - **`person-aged-0-30/31-60/61`**: open dues grouped by days since the claim date. - **`person-overdue-count/-total`**: the count and sum of dues of their overdue claims. - **`person-claims-OPEN-count` / `-SETTLED-count`**: counted over all their claims, not just the live ones. - **`person-score`**: settled total (corrections left out) ÷ 100, minus 5 per overdue claim, rounded half-even to a whole number. **`person-band`** is HIGH, MID or LOW against `score-mid` / `score-high`. - **`person-active`**: they have an open live claim dated within the last 30 days. - **`person-backing`**: for each patron, their SETTLED `settledDue` over the last 90 days times their share, rounded half-even. Shares split 100 equally (`patronShares`), with the remainder going to the first-named patron. - **`person-cut-total`**: the sum of their pool cuts (`PoolRepository.cut`). - A pool cuts only when its shares total exactly 100.00 and it has a pot. - A member gets a cut only if they are current, not retired and not held. Retired or held members get 0.00, and their share goes to the rest. - The rounding remainder goes to the smallest cut. - A future retirement date already removes the cut. - **`person-period-

-due-total` / `-carried`**: - For a closed or soft-closed period, the figure frozen by `PeriodClosing.fixNow`. - Otherwise the front end works it out live, using each claim's status at the period end, read by regex from the status log. - Carried is the person's opening balance plus open claims from earlier periods. - **Statement fields** (`person-statement-count`, `-stated-total`, `-statement-date`): - `TakeStatement` binds each live claim to its current due. Any claim not live is unbound. - When the statement is taken now, the total it computes is thrown away and Rollup's due-total is stored instead. An as-of statement keeps its own total, which ignores shares. - Cancelling a statement (steward only) unbinds every bound claim and does not restore earlier bindings. - **Flags and other fields**: - **`person-flag-shown`**: shown while today is on or before the flag's until-date. While in force, only a steward may open the person's claims. - **`person-retired`**: true whenever a retirement date is set. - `-grade` is the grade in force today. `-terms`, `-contact`, `-clashing`, `-origin` and `-approver` are shown as stored. - **Sheet totals** (`rollup-*`, `header-*`, `consolidated-*`): `trimmedSum` drops the single highest and lowest figure when there are 3 or more. **`rollup-claimed-total` is not trimmed**, nor are the aged totals. ### What is frozen, and when - **Settle** (`SettleClaim`): `settledDue` = the due shown at that moment, late charge included. - "Settle as of" a date freezes the due as an as-of view of that day works it out. - With no rate, nothing is fixed and the due stays live. - **Resettle** (steward) fixes it again at today's figure. - **Approve** (`ApproveClaim`): freezes the due the same way. It is the same code, copied inline. - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`): binds `statedDue` on each claim and keeps the person's stated total. - **Close or soft-close a period** (`PeriodClosing.fixNow`): freezes per-person totals, carried figures and pool cuts. - Its late charge is priced at the sheet's **today**, not the period end. It applies no cap and no shares, unlike Rollup. - **Auto-close** runs when today changes and `grace-days` is set. - **Reopen** (permission `reopen`, refused while the period is locked) drops the frozen figures. - **Changing the sheet's today** writes a SNAPSHOT of each person's due-total, an as-of copy of the schema, and releases every editor lock. - **Rollover** (steward) makes next year's months and puts open figures in as openings, using a *third* copy of the due loop (`RollOver.openFigures`), which leaves out existing openings. **Undo rollover** does not reopen the periods the rollover soft-closed. ### What a closed period changes - `PeriodRepository.requireOpen` refuses about 20 claim actions when the claim's **due-by** falls in a closed period. Soft-closed periods are not blocked; claims added to one are only marked late entry. - A period **cap** limits how many open claims a person may have in it; it is checked only when a claim is opened. ### Who may do what - **Roles** (`RoleRepository.roleOf`): clerk (the default), steward, viewer, restricted. An active **delegation** makes a user a steward. - **`RefuseViewer`**: a YAML guard on most writes. It refuses viewers and archived sheets, but it is missing on several routes, including the bulk actions, grade merge, period lock/unlock and rollover. - **The `Permissions` matrix**, which a `perm-` setting can override: - open, settle, void, close: clerk and steward - reassign, reopen: steward - today: clerk, steward and restricted - **Hard-coded steward-only actions**: re-date, set due-by, review, assign review, waive, resettle, void a SETTLED claim within 7 days (`VoidClaim.SETTLED_DAYS`), flag, merge, transfer, cancel a statement, lock/unlock, rollover, archive, clone, withdraw a rate, merge grades. - **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim or last edited it may not settle or approve it. - **Approve and reject**: a steward, or the person's **approver**. - **Clerk limit**: when a clerk settles a claim whose due is above `clerk-limit[-]` (as in force on the claim's date), it goes to PENDING instead. ⚠ The Javadoc says "on today". - **Thresholds** checked against the claim's due: - `proof-threshold`: no settle or approve without proofs, or without one of each kind when `proof-kinds` is set. - `note-threshold`: no open with an empty note. - `max-open`: a limit on each person's open claims. - **Gaps:** any clerk can set roles (including making themselves steward), name themselves a person's approver, or change settings. The restricted role is only filtered in the UI. ### What a date decides - **Retirement**: a claim dated *after* the retire date is refused. Once today reaches it, the person's unbound open claims leave the totals. - **Defaults**: a blank claim date means `entry-date`, else today. - **Dated settings** (`DatedSetting.on`): floor, late-pct, terms, cap, the thresholds and rounding all go by the claim's date. Grade and terms go by `gradeOn` / `termsOn`. - **Statements** can be taken as of a past date. ### Imports, paste, holds - **Person import** (`ImportPeople`): new people are added, matched people (by name or alias) are updated. - All or nothing. - A blank grade means the default grade, which **regrades** a person who already exists. - Any name clash in the tree or reused contact refuses the whole import. - **Paste** (`PasteClaims`): all or nothing. - It matches an existing DRAFT by date and note, otherwise adds a new claim. - Then it opens every claim as the open button would, so some may go to REVIEW. - Negative lines are always refused. - **Rate import**: all or nothing. A rate dated today or later is forward-only. - **Openings import**: *adds* to the stored openings, even on closed periods. - **Holds** (person or claim): affect only pool cuts. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It is scattered and tangled. No new developer could pick it up from one place. - **Every figure rule exists twice.** The browser computes what you see, and Java recomputes it in four slightly different loops (Rollup, TakeStatement, PeriodClosing, RollOver) with different cap, share and date rules. - **The same lookups are pasted all over.** The rate/floor/late lookup appears in about 10 classes. - **Permissions come from three schemes**: the matrix, hard-coded steward checks, and YAML guards. - **The comments have drifted.** Doc comments, YAML headers and migration notes contradict the code in more than a dozen places, for example when a claim is numbered, which terms fix the due-by, and what a hold does.
